messages:
sasha: Heads up — ran stress benches on the 8xA100 cluster after the channel-crediting change and saw a reproducible throughput drop + tail spike.

sasha: Before: ~4.5k tok/s steady, 95p ~120ms. After: ~3.4k tok/s, 95p ~270ms. CPU/GPU utilization looks fine. KV cache hit rate unchanged.

kevin: Can you attach the trace/profile from perf-tool? curious if it's compute bound or blocked on all-reduce.

sasha: Pasted key snippets from the recorder below. Note the long idle gaps right after forward kernel finishes.
```
# perf timeline (abbrev)
FWD_KERNEL  : 0.0 - 2.1ms
KV_PREFETCH : 2.1 - 2.3ms
ALLREDUCE   : 2.3 - 5.8ms  <-- long
KV_APPLY    : 5.8 - 6.1ms
NEXT_FWD    : 6.2 - 8.3ms
```

jia: That looks like credit/backpressure on the LL128 proto. When channel-crediting reduced inflight windows, we saw the runtime stall waiting for remote credits which looks like these long allreduce segments. Does the trace include nccl event tags?

ryan: It does. nccl timestamps show repeated retries on the same comm step and channel switching every few iterations (channel 0->3->1), which increases latency due to pipeline misalignment.

perf-bot: perf-bot: nightly-regression:channel-crediting - test=8gpu-resnet - delta=-24% throughput - alerted to eng-runtime.

kevin: Quick hypothesis: with smaller per-channel credits the selector/launcher batches are packing slightly different micro-batches, pushing more partial reductions and preventing compute/comm overlap. Two levers to test: 1) bump per-channel credit, 2) force deterministic channel pinning for LL128 to keep steady channel ordering.

jia: Also check kernel selector warmup: if kernel selection shifts between iterations (int8 vs float16 kernel paths), KV cache prefetch timing can move and break overlap. Maybe warmup path regression combined w/ credit change.

ryan: I ran a narrow canary toggling NCCL_PROTO=LL and NCCL_PROTO=LL128. Observations: LL (proto fallback) restores throughput to ~4.4k, LL128 stays low. So it's not a GPU compute kernel perf bug; it's comm pattern.

kevin: Commands I used to toggle for the canary: 
```
export NCCL_PROTO=LL128
export NCCL_ALGO=tree  # test
# or
export NCCL_PROTO=LL
export NCCL_ALGO=ring
```

jia: For a quick mitigation we can: 1) increase NCCL_UNIQUE_ID window/credits in the runtime, 2) implement a channel-sticky mode for LL128 during steady-state, 3) add a small jitter to kernel selector warmup so all workers converge to the same kernel early.

sasha: Which of those is lowest risk to deploy to Dedicated? I want a canary tomorrow.

kevin: Low risk: make channel-sticky mode opt-in and default off, flip on in perf-config for canary pools. Medium risk: bump credits globally (affects memory/backpressure). High risk: change warmup jitter heuristics.

ryan: Also logged a reproducible single-run flame: large spikes at rank boundaries coincident with channel switches. Sample numbers attached inline: iteration 120-140 shows per-iter variance up to 40ms in allreduce start time.

perf-bot: perf-bot: test-logs uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/2301/channel-crediting/2301234567/ (links in thread).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created canary cluster redwood-dev-8g-canary with channel-sticky toggle enabled. patch: runtime/comm/nccl_router: add NCCL_CHANNEL_STICKY=true guard.

jia: I'll PR a short patch to enable sticky channels behind a flag and add a unit test for channel ordering determinism.

kevin: I'll run the canary with and without KV prefetch (toggle runtime.kv.prefetch=false) to see if overlap improves.

sasha: Plan agreed: canary config owner=kevin, observe 6h, rollback if 95p latency worsens. If good, we roll to additional reserved pools and follow up with a permanent fix in kernel selection/warmup.

ryan: I'll collect microbenchmarks for channel credit windows (range 4..64) and post numbers. Early note: credits>=32 starts matching pre-change throughput on LL128.

sasha: Great. Please post exact commands and perf snippets here so we can capture in the postmortem. :thumbsup:
